newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: RESEARCH ALERT-Sell Philippine stocks-Asia Equity.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT-Sell Philippine stocks-Asia Equity.

text.p: "Sell the Philippines" said brokerage Asia Equity to clients on Friday in an advisory in which it recommended a sell on Philippine stocks.

"Heady earnings expectations of 30 percent can only disappoint. And interest rates are too low ... Our sell view on the market is predicated on valuation and earnings expectations," the brokerage said.
The recommendations made by Asia Equity's chief strategist Ian MacFarlene, a copy of which was seen by Reuters, said the market was already fully valued and interest rates were too low.

"Heady earnings expectations of 30 percent havily focused on the property sector, mean the only possible surprise is an unpleasant one. And among the large stocks we have only four firm buys," it said.

"The quality of earnings is also questionable. Strip out the impact of property and earnings would halve to just over 15 percent for the year. Almost every company in the Philippines has an exposure to the property sector. Even Meralco and San Miguel are currently deriving around 10 percent of their earnings from this source," the report said.
"In this environment only big capitalisation stocks such as PNB, PLDT, Aboitiz and Filinvest Land are rated as strong buys," it said.
In the past two sessions Philippine stocks have recovered from a seven-day losing streak that was led by property stocks.
From March 31 until Tuesday, the Philippine Stock Exchange's main index lost more than nine percent.
On Friday, the main index ended at 2,976.78 points, up 27.76 points following the previous day's 39.72 points gain. The market was closed for a holiday on Wednesday.
The weekend trading saw the real estate sector bucking the trend with the property stocks sub-index falling by 7.74 points to 1,417.93.
Property stocks were battered due to persistent fears of a crash in real estate prices due to a glut.
A senior Philippine banker on Thursday sought to allay the fears over rising defaults in Philippine property loans.
"The reports that are coming out are rather overblown, and tend to create a sense of gloom and doom," outgoing president of the Bankers' Association of the Philippines said.
